fatal_errors: The hypothesis concerns heat-treated HfNbTiVAl10 hierarchical heterostructures under tensile and fracture testing, whereas the target study concerns composition screening and as-cast room-temperature compression of Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 against equimolar NbMoTaVW.
It replaces the target intervention—rule-of-mixtures modulus validation followed by VEC/modulus/density screening of 38,326 compositions—with an unreported APT-plus-machine-learning workflow.
The proposed SRO-controlled mechanism does not reconstruct the target VEC–Peierls barrier–dislocation mobility mechanism.
The claimed 15–20% RMSE reduction and minutes-versus-days speedup have no direct support in the cited evidence.
None of the cited sources validates the proposed model for HfNbTiVAl10 fracture behavior or demonstrates superiority over matched finite-element or molecular-dynamics baselines.
explanation: This is a testable research proposal, but it does not agree with the hidden paper in material system, intervention, loading mode, mechanism, baseline, or outcome. The target result was a single-phase BCC Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 alloy with 35.7% compressive fracture strain, 1115 MPa yield strength, and 2550 MPa compressive strength after composition screening based on modulus, VEC, and density. The supplied evidence only establishes that APT can quantify SRO in CoCrNi and that ML can predict compression properties in broader BCC/BCC+B2 datasets; it does not support the material-specific accuracy and efficiency claims. The proposed experiment has some discriminating value, but heat treatment may alter grain size, phases, defects, and residual stress alongside SRO, and its falsification rule is not a clean predeclared independent-validation criterion because it combines several alternatives and does not specify a held-out dataset, baseline implementation, or fracture metric.
